deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the goniometric measurements on a Pistacit (epidote) crystal begun on the previous page, headed 'Aug. 8/9'. On that page each face is listed with five pieces of information:
- its theodolite reading;
- its width;
- its index triple (p,q,r) in system III, referred to a ternary form;
- its index triple in system IV, referred to the form with A=1, B=4.4309, C=2.023;
- its letter in the notations of Kupffer and Mohs.
The next page (170) gives the theory used. For a ternary form whose adjoint is (A,B,C;0,D,0), the inclination i of face (1,0,0) to face (p,q,r) satisfies
cot i = (A p + D r)/sqrt(A B q^2 + (A C - D^2) r^2).
When D=0 this becomes cot i = p/sqrt((B/A) q^2 + (C/A) r^2).

STEP 1: the index transformation III -> IV.
Every pair on this page and the previous one satisfies, up to a common factor (my inference, verified on all pairs):
(u,v,w) = ((p+q)/2, (p-q)/2, r/2).
- Section 4: (13,3,8)->(8,5,4); (5,3,8)->(4,1,4); (-5,3,8)->(-1,-4,4); (-13,-3,8)->(-8,-5,4); (-1,0,0)->(-1,-1,0) after rescaling; (1,0,0)->(1,1,0) after rescaling.
- Section 5b: (-3,-3,4)->(-3,0,2); (1,-3,4)->(-1,2,2); (3,-3,4)->(0,3,2).
- Section 6: (-11,-3,8)->(-7,-4,4); (-5,-3,8)->(-4,-1,4); (-3,-3,8)->(-3,0,4); (5,-3,8)->(1,4,4); (11,-3,8)->(4,7,4).
So column IV is a unimodular-up-to-2 change of axes (a=(p+q)/2, b=(p-q)/2).

STEP 2: the zone symbols.
All faces of one series contain the common q,r part, i.e. they have the form (p, ±3, 8) or (p, -3, 4). They therefore lie in the zone of (1,0,0) and (0,q,r), whose zone axis is the cross product (1,0,0)x(0,q,r) = (0,-r,q).
- Section 4 (q,r)=(3,8) gives (0,-8,3). Gauss writes '0.8.-3'.
- Section 5/5b (q,r)=(-3,4) gives zone [0.4.3]. Gauss writes '0.4.3'.
- Section 6 (q,r)=(-3,8) gives zone [0.8.3]. This is boxed.

STEP 3: the readings.
- Section 4. Readings 0, 45°3', 69°8'30", 110°53'40", 135°0', 179°39'30". The zone is nearly symmetric: 45.05+135.0 ≈ 180 and 69.14+110.89 ≈ 180. Section 4b repeats it: 44°58'40", 69°9', 110°58'30", 134°47', 179°49'.
- Section 5. A first attempt with heavy deletions; the index -3.3.4 is corrected. Section 5b repeats it with readings 180°4', 250°36'20", 276°50', 289°32'. Faces of width 4.5 are noted 'gut reflectirend aber bewachsen' (reflect well but overgrown).
- Section 6. A rough list (257.7, 282.59, 310) is followed by a refined list: 180°16', 229°57'30", 249°20'40", 257°9'20", 291°4'30", 310°24'.

STEP 4: the computation 'Res 9B+64C = (13.0406)^2 = 170.06 ~ 171'.
With A=1, the formula of p.170 gives, for faces (p,-3,8) measured from (-1,0,0), cot i = p/sqrt(9B+64C). Hence sqrt(9B+64C) = p·tan i. My recomputation from the readings:
- Section 4: (13,3,8) at i = 45.05° gives 13.02, so 9B+64C = 169.6. This is the deleted '169.60'.
- Section 6: p=11 at i=49.69° gives sqrt = 12.97.
- Section 6: p=5 at i=69.08° gives sqrt = 13.08.
- Section 6: p=3 at i=76.89° gives sqrt = 12.88.
Gauss settles on 13.0406, i.e. 170.06, and then rounds to 171.

The analogous quantity for zone [0.4.3] is 9B+16C ≈ 72. It is not written; I compute it from 5b, e.g. 3·tan(70.54°) = 8.49.

Combining the two (my step) gives roughly C ≈ 2.04 and B ≈ 3.5 for the III-system form. The page itself only determines 9B+64C.
errors: Section 4: the entry '+13.3.8' at 135° is crossed out. The correct index is -13,-3,8, consistent with IV = -8,-5,4 and with the symmetric position 180-45.
Section 5 (first attempt): the indices +1.3.4 and +3.3.4 are wrong in the sign of q. They are corrected in 5b to +1-3.4 and +3-3.4, consistent with zone [0.4.3].
The rough list in section 6 has '257.7  -3 -3.8'. The intermediate face -5-3.8 (249°20') is missing there and is added in the refined list.

The value 170.06 is not a least-squares mean of the individual determinations (169.6 to 171). Gauss's final '171' indicates an adjustment toward the section-6 faces. The arithmetic (13.0406)^2 = 170.057 is correct.

results.what: Assignment of rational indices to crystal faces in a zone, with conversion between two index systems via (u,v,w) = ((p+q)/2, (p-q)/2, r/2)
results.modern_name: Miller-type indexing and change of crystallographic axes

results.what: Zone axis as cross product of face normals: [0,8,3] and [0,4,3]
results.modern_name: Zone law / zone symbol (Weiss zone law)

results.what: Determination of the metric (adjoint ternary form coefficients) from interfacial angles: cot i = p/sqrt(Bq^2 + Cr^2), giving 9B+64C ≈ 170
results.modern_name: Determination of reciprocal metric tensor from interfacial angles (positive definite quadratic form for the lattice)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's ternary-form treatment of crystallography; general later use by Miller, Bravais

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine goniometric reductions on an epidote crystal. Gauss's use of ternary quadratic forms for crystallography and his crystallographic notes (cf. Werke vol. II/XI, the 'Zur Krystallographie' material) are known. The page is a numerical working sheet with no new theory.
